title: Vanishing on a finite Cartesian grid is a coordinate-polynomial combination
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $A_i\subset K$ be a finite nonempty subset for every $i\in I$. In the polynomial algebra $P=K[t_i:i\in I]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], put $g_i=\prod_{c\in A_i}(t_i-c)$. If $f\in P$ satisfies $f(x)=0$ for every tuple $x\in\prod_{i\in I}A_i$, then there are polynomials $h_i\in P$ such that $f=\sum_{i\in I}g_ih_i$. This includes $I=\varnothing$, where the product of the sets is the singleton empty tuple and the sum is zero.
